dinkum-4.meaning: Every fact survives: "died with his loved ones around him", "They didn't say what day Weir died", "a song the Library of Congress named a national treasure in 1997". The one shift is "had a crack at a solo career", which makes the long solo career sound tentative.
dinkum-4.sense: Terms fit: "muso", "old Grateful Dead mates", "kept his hand in on the Bay Area music scene". "had a crack at a solo career" strains against a career the original calls long.
dinkum-4.authenticity: Natural, understated Australian: "a fixture at Grateful Dead gigs", "with a stint at school in Colorado", "took up the guitar at 13". Nothing bolted on.
dinkum-4.register: Lighter than level 3: the slang is sparse ("muso", "mates", "had a crack", "kept his hand in") and much reads as plain news English, e.g. "Weir played rhythm guitar and sang for the band for decades." No swearing, which suits an obituary.
dinkum-4.tone: Stays a respectful obituary throughout: "announced he'd died with his loved ones around him".
dinkum-4.flow: Reads smoothly: "Weir took up the guitar at 13 and found his way into the local bluegrass scene". "they covered the lot" is a slightly abrupt join.
dinkum-4.variety: Small but unrepeated set: "muso", "mates", "a stint", "had a crack", "covered the lot", "kept his hand in". "musos" appears twice.
dinkum-4.essence: Clearly the same obituary with the same shape and the full list of bands: "Kingfish, Bobby and the Midnites, RatDog".

yarn-dinkum.meaning: Facts kept: "They didn't say what day he died", "an online platform for live shows", "helping people doing it tough". Small shifts: "a fair few of their songs" for "some", and "a fixture at every Grateful Dead concert".
yarn-dinkum.sense: Mostly exact: "for yonks", "a whole swag of other bands", "helping people doing it tough" for poverty relief. "The old Grateful Dead guitarist" can read as aged rather than former, and "had a crack at a solo career" undersells it.
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Sounds like a local: "for yonks", "a whole swag of other bands", "their own outfit", "He'd stayed a regular on the Bay Area music scene".
yarn-dinkum.register: Closest to level 3: steady slang ("yonks", "a fair few", "whole swag", "doing it tough", "outfit") without becoming a yarn, and no swearing at a solemn moment.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Respectful throughout: "let everyone know he'd died with his loved ones around him". "for yonks" is a touch breezy for an obituary but not jarring.
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads well aloud: "which is where he first came across Jerry Garcia playing the banjo". No pile-ups.
yarn-dinkum.variety: The widest spread of the three: "yonks", "a fair few", "solo run", "outfit", "whole swag", "doing it tough", "a regular".
yarn-dinkum.essence: Unmistakably the same obituary, retold: "and that band grew into the Grateful Dead".

dinkum-3.meaning: Every point survives: "has died surrounded by loved ones, his family announced on Saturday", "They didn't say what date he died", "which the Library of Congress named a national treasure in 1997".
dinkum-3.sense: Terms fit: "muso", "went out on his own", "had a crack at everything from country rock", "kept his hand in on the Bay Area music scene, too".
dinkum-3.authenticity: Natural and unforced: "a fixture at every Grateful Dead gig", "grew up round the San Francisco Bay Area", "played in a fair few other groups".
dinkum-3.register: Light for level 3: "muso", "a fair few", "had a crack", "kept his hand in", with much plain news English such as "He played rhythm guitar and sang for the band for decades."
dinkum-3.tone: Keeps the obituary's dignity, opening in news style: "Bob Weir, the American muso and songwriter, has died surrounded by loved ones".
dinkum-3.flow: Smooth and well restructured: "For decades Weir played rhythm guitar and sang with American psychedelic rock band the Grateful Dead".
dinkum-3.variety: Modest but unrepeated: "muso", "bandmates", "a stint", "went out on his own", "a fair few", "had a crack", "kept his hand in".
dinkum-3.essence: Unmistakably the same obituary: "and that grew into the Grateful Dead".
